classification.difficultyReason: Divide each total cost by the number of pears and round the unit price to the nearest cent.

content.prompt: One store at the market advertises pears at 20 for $\$6.00$ and another store 15 for $\$5.00$. Calculate the price per pear at each store. (Round to the nearest cent.)

answer.short: First store: 30 cents per pear. Second store: 33 cents per pear.
answer.worked:
First store:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Price per pear}&=\frac{600}{20}\text{ cents}\\\text{Price per pear}&=30\text{ cents}\end{align*}$$
Second store:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Price per pear}&=\frac{500}{15}\text{ cents}\\\text{Price per pear}&=33\tfrac{1}{3}\text{ cents}\\\text{Price per pear}&\approx33\text{ cents}\end{align*}$$
The prices are 30 cents and 33 cents per pear respectively, to the nearest cent.
